title: Forward Cargo Door Latching Wear Found Earlier Than Expected on Line Checks
abstract: Maintenance organisation request for a more durable forward cargo door latching standard after wear and door warning nuisance messages appeared far earlier in life than the current inspection interval assumes.

sections.request: We maintain a mixed SOLANO fleet for four customers and we are seeing the same forward cargo door problem across all of them. The latch hooks are wearing on the load-bearing face much faster than the interval in the maintenance programme assumes, and once the wear passes a certain point the door warning starts giving spurious open indications on push-back. Crews will not depart with that message, so it becomes a delay. In the last twelve months we have logged thirty-one departure delays traced to this door and eight of them went past fifteen minutes. Replacing the hooks is not a difficult job but the parts are on a long lead time and we cannot keep enough of them on the shelf at outstations. We would prefer a latching standard that lasts the life of the aircraft, or at least one that matches the inspection interval we are given.
sections.background: The current latching standard was fitted to these aircraft in production and there has already been one improvement service bulletin, which we embodied on eleven aircraft between 2019 and 2022. Those aircraft are wearing more slowly but they are not free of it. Our shop findings show the wear concentrating on one side of the hook, which suggests the load is not being shared as designed. The door proximity sensing has been re-rigged twice on two aircraft with no lasting benefit.
sections.expected_outcome: A latching arrangement that does not need a hook change inside the life of the aircraft, that removes the nuisance door warning indications, and that can be fitted at an A-check rather than requiring the door to be removed.

type_data.business_justification: Thirty-one departure delays in twelve months across a twenty-two aircraft managed fleet, plus an AOG spares exposure the customer values at 240 kEUR per year.
